title: Triangles and Rectangles
short: Know a triangle and a rectangle, even when turned.
trouble: Children think a triangle must point up.

blocks.html: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners. A rectangle has 4 sides: two long and two short. A triangle can point any way!

blocks.name: pk-pic
blocks.cap: Two triangles and a rectangle. The turned triangle is still a triangle.

blocks.html: A triangle has 3 sides. A rectangle has 4 sides, two long and two short.

For the grown-up: Make triangles and rectangles with sticks, straws or your fingers. Cut a sandwich into triangles or rectangles and name the shapes before eating. A few problems on the screen is plenty. The real practice is with things you can touch.

items: Try it at home: Cut toast into triangles.
Make shapes with string on the floor.

sources.name: Head Start Early Learning Outcomes Framework (ELOF), Mathematics Development, preschool goals P-MATH 1 to 10
